text: My sister wanted a practice upright before her recital in Lisbon, so we spent Saturday copying what private sellers wanted for instruments that still had every key. A teacher in Alfama asked 2360, a widow in Estrela asked 3980, and a school closing a classroom asked 1840. The shop behind the tram barn wanted 2870 for a German frame, a tuner in Santos wanted 3520, and a church loft was listed at 2100. A damp basement piano stood at 3140, and the last card on the cafe board was 2590. Benches stayed out of the talk.

estimate.instruction: Give the euro amount sitting between the two central asking prices.

place.instruction: Which city were the pianos in?

text: The riad keeper in Fez wanted the courtyard zellige replaced before guests arrived, and he copied every mason onto the back of a sugar packet. The man from the tannery lane said 1490. A cousin offered 780 if the old tiles could be lifted whole. The hotel contractor wrote 2050. A quieter crew from the medina put down 1040, the tile merchant's brother said 640, and a crew that brought its own cement said 1760. The remaining slips were 1280 for labour only and 910 if we carried the sand up ourselves.

estimate.instruction: Give the dirham amount sitting between the two central mason figures.

place.instruction: Which city is the riad in?

text: My uncle wanted a skiff and a skipper for one calm day out of Split, and he made me write down what the harbour men asked. The blue hull wanted 420, an older cousin said 260 if we brought the fuel, the concrete pier asked 510, and a man mending nets asked 370. No one included lunch.

estimate.instruction: Give the euro amount sitting between the two central charter prices.

place.instruction: Which city is the harbour in?
